overall_summary: Space-themed anomalies and extreme biological paradoxes are currently driving the highest views and engagement on the channel. Conversely, abstract cognitive psychology and brain-related facts are underperforming. Additionally, duplicate uploads of identical concepts within a short window show diminishing returns.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Largest Ocean in Space Will Mind-Blow You!' (460 views, 5 likes) and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views, 4 likes) are the top-performing videos in the dataset.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space topics that feature extreme physical environments, weird cosmic chemistry, or massive scale comparisons.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (301 views, 3 likes) and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' (179 views, 3 likes) perform significantly better than standard trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Frame animal facts around survival extremes, evolutionary anomalies, or historical timeline paradoxes.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (39 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) struggle to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely internal, non-visual psychological concepts unless they can be paired with a highly relatable, immediate physical sensation.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded on Sep 4 got 5 views, and the Sep 7 version got 54 views. 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' got 183 views on Sep 5 and 118 views on Sep 7.
weak_patterns.action: Space out similar topics by at least 2-3 weeks instead of repeating them within days to prevent audience fatigue and algorithm suppression.

next_video.concept: The Planet of Burning Ice (Gliese 436 b)
next_video.opening_direction: Show a simulation of a planet covered in ice that is actively blazing with fire, asking: 'How can a planet be made of solid ice, but constantly burn at 800 degrees?'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet's gravity is so incredibly strong that it compresses water molecules into a solid state called Ice VII, preventing it from evaporating despite the scorching heat.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful space category and uses a strong physical paradox hook, similar to our top-performing cosmic and planetary videos.

experiment: Test a 'Time-Scale Paradox' format (e.g., 'Cleopatra lived closer to the iPhone than the building of the Great Pyramid') to see if historical timeline anomalies perform as well as biological and cosmic paradoxes.
